Short story: This video animates the vendor-by-vendor revenue race in the global cloud infrastructure market (IaaS/PaaS/hosted services) from 2006 through 2026. Amazon Web Services went from essentially $0 in 2006 to $25.7B in 2018 and $62.2B by 2021, becoming the early runaway leader. Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud then accelerated, with Azure scaling into the $50–$70B range by the mid-2020s. Alibaba Cloud grew quickly in Asia before slowing. "Others" (dozens of regional providers, telco clouds and private cloud revenues) remain a sizeable chunk of the market.

instagram_caption:
🚀 The $300B+ Battle for The Cloud Throne — who wins the crown?

From a tiny Amazon experiment in 2006 to a 2025 market topping over $300B, the cloud market is the biggest tech power play you’ve probably never fully tracked. Amazon Web Services started as a niche infrastructure project and exploded to $4.6B in 2014, then $25.7B by 2018 — and a jaw-dropping $62.2B in 2021. In our animated timeline you’ll watch AWS sprint ahead, then face a wall of challengers.

Microsoft Azure quietly climbed the ranks: almost invisible in 2010, then scaling into double-digit billions by mid-decade. Our numbers show Azure moving from about $3.25B in 2014 to roughly $44.1B in 2021 and an estimated $68.8B by 2026. Google Cloud followed its own trajectory — slow early years, then a massive push into AI and enterprise that lands it in the $30–45B neighborhood by the mid-2020s.

Alibaba Cloud is the Asia-focused titan in this story: near-zero in the early days, breaking out after 2013 and reaching double-digit billions by 2021. The "Others" bucket — hundreds of niche providers, telcos and regional clouds — remains shockingly large: tens of billions in 2014 and a surge to over $90B+ by 2025 in our timeline.

The turning points: AWS’s early lead (2006–2014), the 2018–2021 acceleration (cloud adoption + pandemic migration), and the 2021–2025 era where competition, AI demand and enterprise migrations rewrite market shares. By 2025 AWS still holds the crown, but Azure and Google Cloud are closing in — and the rest of the market refuses to disappear.

Which shift surprised you most — AWS’s early dominance, Azure’s steady climb, or Google’s late surge? Drop a comment with the year you think changed the game.

Headline: The Cloud Throne — How AWS Built a Kingdom and Who's Closing In

Detailed summary: This timeline visualization traces the global cloud infrastructure market from 2006 to 2026 (2026 = estimate). Amazon Web Services went from near-zero in 2006 to $25.7B in 2018 and $62.2B in 2021. Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud rose behind AWS, with Azure estimated to reach ~$68.8B by 2026 and Google Cloud moving into the $40B range. Alibaba Cloud grew rapidly in Asia and remains a top-five player. The aggregate market expands from single-digit billions in the late 2000s to the low hundreds of billions by the mid-2020s, driven by enterprise cloud adoption, AI workloads, and pandemic-era migrations.

Sources include Amazon annual reports (AWS net sales), public vendor filings, and market-share research from Synergy-style analyst distributions. Figures for 2024–2026 are model-based estimates anchored to public disclosures.
